mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 7% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in the manufacturing sector, which reduces corporate earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four-month INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (inflation) above 3% over two months signals a monetary policy tightening in an inflationary environment, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-over-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 10% signals a collapse in residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related industries and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST falls by more than 10% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A positive and accelerating growth in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200k per month for three consecutive months, combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates labor market imbalances that may precede a policy response; this interaction predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate expansionary policy.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200k for three months AND UNRATE rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS exceeds 200k for three months and UNRATE is rising.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a shift from consumption to saving, which typically precedes a demand slowdown and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is persistently above its 12-month moving average for six months.
